ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r6.claim: God controls joy and grief, life and death, provision and children, prosperity and poverty, so everyone should turn to Him at all times.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r6.anchor: sorrow and happiness, life and death, subsistence and children, affluence and poverty are all under the control of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r3.claim: God moves people from poverty to sufficiency and affluence; Islahi distinguishes the enrichment term from merely emerging from poverty by its sense of accumulated wealth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r3.anchor: which is used for accumulated wealth. So the word

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r4.claim: The wealth of rich people who withhold spending while dreaming of Paradise comes from God, not Sirius, which God also rules.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p69/r4.anchor: the character of those rich people is referred to who, though do not spend in the cause of God

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r10.speaker: الجوهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r10.claim: Al-Jawharī gives the verb qaniya and its pattern, and explains that its transitivity changes with the vowel; the form means acquiring or possessing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r10.anchor: قال الجوهري: قني يقنى قنى، كغني يغنى غنى، ويتعدى بتغيير الحركة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r11.claim: The causative forms aqnāhu and qannāhu mean that God gave him wealth or possessions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r11.anchor: فتقول: أقناه الله مالا، وقناه الله مالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r12.speaker: شاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r12.claim: The poet says some rich people lose their fortune while some formerly poor people acquire wealth, using taqnā for gaining possessions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r12.anchor: كم من غني أصاب الدهر ثروته ... ومن فقير تقنى بعد الإقلال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r13.claim: Aqnāhu may also mean that God satisfied him with what he possessed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r13.anchor: ويقال: أقناه الله مالا، وأرضاه من القنية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r14.speaker: أبو زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r14.claim: Abū Zayd records traditional terms for a gift of one hundred: al-qinā for goats, al-ghinā for sheep, and al-minā for camels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r14.anchor: قال أبو زيد: تقول العرب لمن أعطي مائة من المعز: أعطي القنى، ومن أعطي مائة من الضأن: أعطي الغنى

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.claim: This section then turns to perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.anchor: transitions into a discussion of the perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham

RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r1.claim: “Enriched” means that God removes a person’s need: being free of need in every respect is absolute wealth, while freedom from need in one respect is wealth in that respect.
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r1.anchor: فنقول : { أغنى } يعني دفع حاجته ولم يتركه محتاجا

RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r2.claim: The Prophet’s instruction to make people independent of asking on this day is applied to the alms of breaking the fast: give them what they need.
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r2.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أغنوهم عن المسألة في هذا اليوم ) وحمل ذلك على زكاة الفطر

RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r3.claim: “And bestowed wealth” means giving more than what removes need; al-Rāzī proposes a sound-symbolic fit because qāf is articulated above ghayn and thus suggests a higher state.
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { * أقنى } معناه وزاد عليه الإقناء فوق الإغناء ، والذي عندي أن الحروف متناسبة

RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r4.claim: Need-removing gifts include senses such as sight and speech, nursing in infancy, or necessary food and clothing; what removes need is enrichment, and whatever exceeds it is further bestowal.
RAZI-FULL:v29p20#2/r4.anchor: وفي الجملة كل ما دفع الله به الحاجة فهو إغناء ؛ وكل ما زاد عليه فهو إقناء

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.claim: Except verse 46, each verse in 42–50 begins wa anna, continuing the discussion of Moses’ and Abraham’s scriptures in 36–41.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r1.anchor: Each verse in this passage, except v. 46, begins with wa anna

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.claim: Wa anna may instead be read wa inna, making each instance an independent thought meaning truly, surely, or verily.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r2.anchor: But wa anna could also be read wa inna, which would make each occurrence mark a new, independent thought

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r14.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r14.claim: Most commentators understand the second genesis as resurrection, with human creation from a drop demonstrating God’s ability to resurrect.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r14.anchor: resurrection is what is referred to here as the second genesis, according to most commentators

STUDYQURAN:53:42/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r15.speaker: Al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r15.claim: Al-Rāzī takes the second genesis as the Spirit being breathed into a human, because the Spirit ennobles humans and distinguishes them from other animals.
STUDYQURAN:53:42/r15.anchor: Al-Rāzī, however, understands the second genesis as a reference to the breathing of the Spirit into the human being

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r1.claim: Aghnā means that God enriches people with wealth; aqnā is from qinyah, property kept as a lasting reserve or capital rather than sold.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r1.anchor: أعطى الغنى للناس بالأموال {وأقنى} وأعطى القنية وهي ما يتأثل من الأموال

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r2.claim: Qinyah is wealth acquired for oneself and retained, not traded; Tāj al-maṣādir also glosses the verb as providing capital and contenting.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r2.anchor: بأن يقصد حفظه استثمارا واستنماء وأن لا يخرج عن ملكه

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r3.claim: One view is that God gives people sufficiency and wealth, then gives them stored property beyond what suffices.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : أغنى الناس بالكفاية والأموال وأعطى القنية وما يدخرونه بعد الكفاية

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets enrichment as gold, silver, clothes, and homes, and stored property as camels, cattle, sheep, and livestock.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك : أغنى بالذهب والفضة والثياب والمسكن وأقنى بالإبل والبقر والغنم والدواب

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r5.claim: Other explanations say stored wealth is singled out as the noblest, or that aqnā means God made a person content by making satisfaction his possession.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r5.anchor: وأفراد القنية بالذكر أي بعد قوله أغني لأنها أشرف الأموال وأفضلها أو معنى أقنى أرضى

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r6.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r6.claim: Given the surrounding antitheses, Saʿdī al-Muftī's reading that aqnā means 'made poor' best fits; its hamza marks removal.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r6.anchor: والأوفق لما تقدمه من الآي المشتملة على مراعاة صنعة الطباق أن يحمل على معنى أفقر

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r7.speaker: الجنيد
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r7.claim: Al-Junayd says God enriched some people through Him and impoverished others from Him.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r7.anchor: قال الجنيد قدس سره : أغنى قوما به وأفقر قوما منه

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r8.claim: Some say the verse alludes to God's effusion upon a sound, steady heart and preservation of that light there against the commanding ego's darkness; an unstable heart can lose it.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : فيه إشارة إلى إفاضة الفيض الإلهي على القلب السليم المستقيم الثابت على دين الله

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r9.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r9.claim: The Prophet's prayer asks God to make his heart firm upon His religion, which the Sufi reading relates to preserving divine light in the heart.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r9.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : اللهم ثبت قلبي على دينك

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r10.claim: Bursevī infers permission to acquire useful wealth and prohibition on keeping dogs without a use such as guarding crops or livestock.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r10.anchor: ثم إن الآية دلت على إباحة التأثل من الأموال النافعة دون غيرها ولذا نهى عن اقتناء الكبب

BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r11.claim: He likens the commanding ego to a vicious dog and contrasts it with cultivating a growing spirit rather than keeping something barren and useless.
BURSEVI:v9p209#2/r11.anchor: والنفس الأمارة أشد من الكلب العقوب ففي اقتناى الروح النامي مندوحة عن اقتنائها أبتر عقيم لا خير فيها

TABATABAI:53:40-43/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r14.claim: Exclusive divine causation does not rule out natural or non-natural intermediaries such as human joy, organs of laughter, angels, or other causes; these are subject to God and not independent.
TABATABAI:53:40-43/r14.anchor: ولا ينافي ما في هذه الموارد من الحصر توسط أسباب أخر طبيعية أو غير طبيعية فيها

TABATABAI:53:43-49/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r13.claim: Aghna means that God gave wealth or sufficiency, while aqna means that He gave lasting possessions such as a house, garden, or livestock; mentioning the particular after the general honors it.

TABATABAI:53:43-49/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r14.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r14.claim: A reported alternative defines enriching as providing funds and aqna as making the recipient content with them.
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r14.anchor: وقيل الإغناء التمويل والإقناء الإرضاء بذلك

TABATABAI:53:43-49/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r15.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r15.claim: Some say the phrase means that God makes people rich and poor.
TABATABAI:53:43-49/r15.anchor: وقال بعضهم معنى الآية أنه هو أغنى وأفقر

TABATABAI:53:33-62/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r13.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r13.claim: Imam Ali explains that God provides every person a livelihood and makes the person content with what his hands earn.
TABATABAI:53:33-62/r13.anchor: قال قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى }

TABRISI:53:42-43/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:42-43/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:42-43/r5.claim: Aqnā derives from qinya, lasting principal property kept for oneself; iqtināʾ is keeping something permanently, and qanāh is connected because it is retained.
TABRISI:53:42-43/r5.anchor: وأقنى من القنية وهي أصل المال وما يقتنى

TABRISI:53:44-51/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:44-51/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
TABRISI:53:44-51/r6.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ explains that God enriches people with wealth and grants them lasting property and principal wealth beyond what they need.
TABRISI:53:44-51/r6.anchor: أي أغنى الناس بالأموال وإعطاء القنية وأصول المال

TABRISI:53:44-51/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:44-51/r7.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:53:44-51/r7.claim: Al-Hasan, Mujāhid, and Qatāda explain aqnā as giving servants.
TABRISI:53:44-51/r7.anchor: وقيل: أقنى أي أخدم عن الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:53:44-51/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:44-51/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:53:44-51/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains aghnā as making rich and aqnā as making content with what one is given.
TABRISI:53:44-51/r8.anchor: أغنى مول وأقنى أرضى بما أعطى عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:53:44-51/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:44-51/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:53:44-51/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd offers the contrasting explanation that God impoverishes and deprives whomever He wills.
TABRISI:53:44-51/r9.anchor: وأقنى أي أفقر وحرم من شاء عن ابن زيد

THALABI:v9p156/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p156/r4.speaker: أبو الصلاح
THALABI:v9p156/r4.claim: Abū al-Ṣalāḥ says God enriched people with money and gave them a female singer and capital assets.
THALABI:v9p156/r4.anchor: قال أبو الصلاح: أغنى الناس بالمال، وأقنى: أعطى القينة وأصول الأموال

THALABI:v9p156/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p156/r5.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v9p156/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God enriched people with gold, silver, and kinds of property, and gave them camels, sheep, and cattle.
THALABI:v9p156/r5.anchor: الضحاك: أغنى بالذهب والفضة وصنوف الأموال، وأقنى بالإبل والغنم والبقر

THALABI:v9p156/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p156/r6.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وقتادة
THALABI:v9p156/r6.claim: Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda gloss أقنى as providing servants.

THALABI:v9p156/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p156/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p156/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, also in a narration from Mujāhid, glosses أقنى as making a person content with what God has given.
THALABI:v9p156/r7.anchor: ابن عباس: أرضى بما أعطى، وهي رواية بن أبي نجيح وليث عن مجاهد

THALABI:v9p156/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p156/r8.speaker: سليمان التيمي
THALABI:v9p156/r8.claim: Sulaymān al-Taymī, transmitting from al-Ḥaḍramī, says God is self-sufficient and has made creatures dependent on Him.
THALABI:v9p156/r8.anchor: سليمان التيمي عن الحضرمي: أغنى نفسه وأفقر الخلائق إليه

THALABI:v9p156/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p156/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v9p156/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says أغنى means increased and أقنى means reduced, citing God's extension and restriction of provision.
THALABI:v9p156/r9.anchor: ابن زيد: أغنى: أكثر وأفقر: أقل، وقرأ يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر

THALABI:v9p156/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p156/r10.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v9p156/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses أقنى as making poor.

THALABI:v9p156/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p156/r11.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v9p156/r11.claim: Ibn Kaysān glosses أقنى as giving offspring.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r1.claim: God enriches people with wealth and supplies them with funds.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r2.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says aqnā means giving acquired property and assets kept for future use.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r2.anchor: فقال أبو صالح: أعطى القنية وأصول الأموال التي تقتنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r3.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل وعكرمة عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r3.claim: The majority, including Mujāhid, Muqātil, and ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās, say aqnā means making a poor person content with what was given.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r3.anchor: والاكثرون قالوا: أقنى قنع ورضى بما أعطى الفقير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة والمبرد وابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda, al-Mubarrad, and Ibn al-Aʿrābī prefer the first sense: giving people enduring property or a reserve.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r4.anchor: والقول الأول اختيار أبي عبيدة، والمبرد، وابن الأعرابي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r5.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r5.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī glosses aqnā as giving what can be stored after basic needs are met.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: أقنى أعطاه ما يدخر بعد الكفاية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq mentions both main interpretations, which al-Wāḥidī says return to one underlying root.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r6.anchor: وأبو إساق ذكر القولين (¬4)، وهما يرجعان إلى أصل واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r7.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r7.claim: Al-Layth says qaniytu bihi means being content with it and aqnaytu property means making it a valued reserve; a line by al-Mutalammis uses aqnū for contentment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r7.anchor: قال الليث: يقال: قنيت به، أي: رضيت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r8.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r8.claim: A second poetic usage gives aqnū the sense “I retain and preserve,” supporting a root of keeping and holding.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r9.speaker: الضحاك والحسن وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda say God enriches through money and gives servants as property, restricting aqnā to servants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r9.anchor: قال الضحاك، والحسن، وقتادة: أغنى في المال وأقنى في الخدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says aghnā means increased and aqnā means decreased; al-Wāḥidī rejects “decreased” as linguistically unsupported unless it means contentment with little.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p73/r10.anchor: وأما ما روي عن ابن زيد أنه قال: أغنى أكثر وأقنى أقل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r3.claim: God enriches people with money; one explanation of aqna is that He makes them content with what He has given.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r3.anchor: وأنه هو أغنى } بالمال { وأقنى } أرضى بما أعطى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r4.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r4.claim: An alternative meaning of aqna is that God gives principal assets and property kept as lasting wealth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:46-50/r4.anchor: أرضى بما أعطى. وقيل: أقنى: أعطى أصول الأموال وما يتخذ فيه قنية

ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r21.claim: The phrase means that God enriches the poor and supplies capital, freeing them from need; it may also mean that He makes them content, as in 93:8.
ELMALILI:53:33-54#2/r21.anchor: fakir olan bir kulunu ihtiyaçtan kurtarıp sermayedâr eden, yahut hoşnut eyleyen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.claim: Verses 43–49 give examples showing that all events across life and death, and all that happens in the universe, depend on God’s will and power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r8.anchor: insanın hayat-ölüm çizgisi içinde cereyan eden her oluşun ve evrende olup biten her şeyin Allah Teâlâ’nın irade ve kudretine bağlı bulunduğunu gösteren örnekler verilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r11.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r11.claim: Al-Shawkānī also understands the verse as saying that God makes people wealthy and makes them poor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r11.anchor: 48. âyet “Zengin eden de O’dur, yoksul kılan da” şeklinde de anlaşılmıştır (Şevkânî

BURHAN:v2p449/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p449/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p449/r3.claim: The pronoun هو between إن and its predicate marks these acts as God's alone, since others may claim to give life or cause death; it is omitted for creating the sexes, which no one can claim.
BURHAN:v2p449/r3.anchor: فورد في هذه الجمل الاربع الفصل بالضمير المرفوع بين اسم إن وخبرها

ITQAN:v2p372/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p372/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p372/r3.claim: أغنى means freeing from poverty and أقنى making one content with wealth; عنترة العبسي’s line witnesses أقنى.
ITQAN:v2p372/r3.anchor: قال أغنى من الفقر وأقنى من الغنى فقنع به

SULAMI:v2p289#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p289#3/r1.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
SULAMI:v2p289#3/r1.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna transmits the wording as “He enriched, granted possession, and pleased,” without further glossing its terms.
SULAMI:v2p289#3/r1.anchor: سفيان بن عيينة يقول : في قوله : أغنى وأقنى وأرضى

SULAMI:v2p289#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p289#3/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p289#3/r2.claim: God enriches some people through Himself and impoverishes others by their being apart from Him.
SULAMI:v2p289#3/r2.anchor: قال الجنيد في قوله : ﴿ وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى ﴾ قال : اغنى قوما به وافقر قوما عنه

TUSTARI:53:48/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:53:48/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:53:48/r1.claim: The outward sense concerns worldly provision; inwardly, God enriches through obedience and makes poor through disobedience.
TUSTARI:53:48/r1.anchor: ظاهرها متاع الدنيا، وباطنها أغنى بالطاعة وأفقر بالمعصية

TUSTARI:53:48/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:53:48/r2.speaker: ابن عيينة
TUSTARI:53:48/r2.claim: Ibn Uyayna explains the words as making someone content and satisfied.
TUSTARI:53:48/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عيينة: أغنى وأقنى أي أقنع وأرضى

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p430/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p430/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p430/r1.claim: Aqna means that God gave what can be possessed, from qinya and property; one says “I acquired this,” or “God made me acquire it.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p430/r1.anchor: {وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى} [أي أعطى ما يقتنى] : من القنية والنشب. يقال: أقنيت كذا [وأقنانيه الله] .

MAJAZ:v2p238/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p238/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p238/r6.claim: He enriched some people and gave them possessions or principal wealth.
MAJAZ:v2p238/r6.anchor: أغنى أقواما وجعل لهم قنية أصل مال

NAHHAS:v4p278/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p278/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p278/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains aqnā as satisfied or made content.
NAHHAS:v4p278/r5.anchor: روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال أقنى أرضى

NAHHAS:v4p278/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p278/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
NAHHAS:v4p278/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says God made some of creation rich and left others poor.
NAHHAS:v4p278/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد أغنى بعض خلقه وأفقر بعضهم

NAHHAS:v4p278/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p278/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p278/r7.claim: Al-Nahhas says aqnā means keeping something as a lasting possession, so God grants enduring wealth.
NAHHAS:v4p278/r7.anchor: يقال أقنيت الشيء أي اتخذته عندي وجعلته مقيما فأقنى جعل له مالا مقيما

SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses أقنى as giving retained property that one has accumulated and resolved not to release.
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " أعطى القنية وهي المال الذي تأثلته وعزمت أن لا يخرج من يدك

SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r2.speaker: الجوهري
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r2.claim: Al-Jawharī gives قني يقنى قنى like غني يغنى غنى; قنيت مالا means acquiring wealth, and causatives can take a second object.
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r2.anchor: قال الجوهري: " قني الرجل يقنى قنى، مثل: غني يغنى غنى ". ثم يتعدى

SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r3.claim: An unnamed poetic line uses تقنى for acquiring wealth, with مالا understood as an omitted second object.

SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r4.claim: The objects of أغنى and أقنى are omitted because the point is to attribute these acts to God alone, as with following verbs.
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r4.anchor: وحذف مفعولا أغنى وأقنى؛ لأن المراد نسبة هذين الفعلين إليه وحده

SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r5.claim: The alif of أقنى comes from yāʾ because the word derives from القنية; a line supports this form.
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r5.anchor: وألف " أقنى " عن ياء لأنه من القنية قال:

SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r6.claim: Another reported gloss takes أقنى to mean أرضى.
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r6.anchor: وقيل: أقنى أرضى. قال الراغب: " وتحقيقه: أنه

SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r7.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib explains أرضى as making contentment an acquired possession.
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r7.anchor: قال الراغب: " وتحقيقه: أنه جعل له قنية من الرضا

SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:48/r8.claim: The cited line uses قنيت for possessing modesty as chastity and nobility.

ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r5.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r5.claim: One gloss of أقنى is made content or satisfied.

ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r6.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r6.claim: Another gloss is that God gave someone lasting property; أقتنيت describes acquiring something to keep and not let go.
ZAJJAJ:v5p76/r6.anchor: والآخر (أقنى) جعل له قنية، أي جعل الغنى أصلا لصاحبه ثابتا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God made people free from poverty and gave contentment from wealth; he cites Antara's imperative aqni as Arabic evidence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أغنى من الفقر وأقني من الغنى فقنع. واستشهد بقول عنترة العبسي

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r4.speaker: عنترة العبسي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r4.claim: Antara's line 'fa-aqni haya'aka' is cited as evidence for the sense of contentment or restraint in aqna.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r4.anchor: فاقْنَىْ حياءك لا أبَالكِ واعْلمى. . . أني امرؤ سأموتُ إن لم أُقْتَلِ

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r5.claim: Aqna is unique in form and root in the Qur'an; the related w-root appears in qinwan in 6:99.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r5.anchor: وحيدة في القرآن، صيغة ومادة. ومن الواوى جاءت {قِنْوَانٌ} في آية الأنعام 99

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r6.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r6.claim: Al-Raghib says aqna means giving wealth and possessions kept as property; another gloss is contentment, understood as a store of satisfaction and obedience.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r6.anchor: قال الراغب: اي أعطى منه الغني وما فيه القنية، أي المال المدخر. وقيل: أقني وأرضى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r7.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r7.claim: In the hadith about God loving a servant, Ibn al-Athir explains iqtnāh as taking the servant as one's chosen favorite.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p546/r7.anchor: قال ابن الأثير: اي اتخذه واصطفاه

NASHR:v2p81/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p81/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr opens the listed non-verse-final words on the routes that incline verse endings; for موسى he follows his usual between-vowels reading where imāla is transmitted.
NASHR:v2p81/r7.anchor: فإن أبا عمرو يفتح جميع ذلك من طريق المميلين له رءوس الآي لأنه ليس برأس آية

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#3/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as God enriching and providing servants.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ أغنى وأقنى ﴾ أغنى وأخدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r1.claim: Aqnā means to acquire or furnish possessions for keeping: qaniytu al-māl is to acquire wealth, and aqnaytuhu is to provide it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r1.anchor: وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى: أي أكسب القنية، يقال: قنيت المال: أي كسبته، وأقنيته إياه: أي أكسبته إياه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r2.claim: The objects of “enriches” and “provides possessions” are omitted because the point is to attribute both actions to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r2.anchor: ولم يذكر متعلق أغنى وأقنى لأن المقصود نسبة هذين الفعلين له تعالى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r3.claim: Exegetes offer twelve explanations; since none is demonstrably the uniquely intended one, they should be treated as examples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r3.anchor: وقد تكلم المفسرون على ذلك فقالوا اثني عشر قولا، كقولهم: أغنى نفسه وأفقر خلقه إليه، وكل قول منها لا دليل على تعينه، فينبغي أن تجعل أمثلة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r11.claim: The emphatic هو distinguishes God as the true agent of laughter, weeping, death, life, enrichment, and provision, despite human claims to such power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p25#2/r11.anchor: ففي الثلاثة الأول، لما كان قد يدعي ذلك بعض الناس، كقول نمروذ: أنا أحيي وأميت

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r1.claim: Aqna means that God bestowed possessions that remain and endure, such as gardens, livestock, and buildings; these precious assets merit separate mention despite being included in enrichment.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r1.anchor: وأعطى القنية وهو ما يبقى ويدوم من الأموال ببقاء نفسه أو أصله كالرياض والحيوان والبناء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r2.claim: In Arabic, qaniya al-māl means he acquired wealth; the verb also occurs with the hamza or doubled consonant, as aqnāhu or qannāhu.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r2.anchor: قنيت المال أي كسبته ويعدى أيضابالهمزة والتضعيف

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses aghnā as making someone wealthy and aqnā as making him content.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ( أغنى ) مول ( وأقنى ) أرضى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r4.claim: Al-Raghib explains contentment as a figurative form of possession: God gives a reserve of contentment and obedience, the greatest of treasures.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r4.anchor: الراغب : وتحقيق ذلك أنه جعل له قنية منالرضا والطاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد والأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd and al-Akhfash understand aqnā as impoverishing, treating the hamza as privative, as in ashkā.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r5.anchor: وعن ابن زيد والأخفش ( اقتنى ) أفقر ووجه بأنهما جعلا الهمزة فيه للسلب والإزالة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r6.claim: A different explanation of impoverishing takes aqnā as giving contentment and patience as one's lasting possession, preserving the pairing of opposites like causing death and life or laughter and tears.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : إنهما جعلا ( أقنى ) بمعنى جعل له الرضا والصبر قنية كناية عن ذلك ليظهر فيه الطباق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r7.speaker: الحضرمي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r7.claim: Al-Hadrami says God enriched Himself and made creatures poor before Him; al-Ālūsī objects that applying the implicit object this way sounds awkward and risks a wrong implication, and says the object is omitted because the acts themselves are the focus.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p69#2/r7.anchor: وفسره بأفقر أيضا الحضرمي إلا أنه كما أخرج عنه ابن جرير وأبو الشيخ قال ( أغنى ) نفسه سبحانه و ( أفقر ) الخلائق إليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r1.claim: He enriches people with money and gives them retained property and capital beyond what they need.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r1.anchor: قال أبو صالح: أغنى الناس بالأموال وأقنى أي: أعطى القنية وأصول الأموال وما يدخرونه بعد الكفاية.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r2.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r2.claim: He enriches with gold, silver, and kinds of wealth, and gives livestock as possessions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r2.anchor: قال الضحاك: أغنى بالذهب والفضة وصنوف الأموال، وأقنى بالإبل والبقر والغنم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r3.speaker: قتادة والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r3.claim: Qatāda and Ḥasan explain aqnā as making someone a servant or providing service.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God gives and thereby satisfies.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: "أغنى وأقنى": أعطى فأرضى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r5.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r5.claim: Mujāhid and Muqātil explain aqnā as making people content with what He gives and satisfied.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد ومقاتل: "أقنى": أرضى بما أعطى وقنع.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd explains aghnā as giving more and aqnā as giving less, citing God's expansion and restriction of provision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: "أغنى": أكثر "وأقنى": أقل وقرأ: "يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر"،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r7.speaker: الأخفش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash takes aqnā to mean making poor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r7.anchor: وقال الأخفش: "أقنى": أفقر. وقال ابن كيسان: أولد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r8.speaker: ابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r8.claim: Ibn Kaysān takes aqnā to mean causing someone to have children.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p419/r8.anchor: وقال الأخفش: "أقنى": أفقر. وقال ابن كيسان: أولد.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r3.claim: Aqnā means God gave lasting possessions, singular because enduring property is the noblest kind of wealth.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r4.claim: Alternatively, it means ‘He pleased’; God makes contentment a person's lasting possession.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:47-50/r4.anchor: أو أرضى وتحقيقه جعل الرضا له قنية

BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r9.claim: True richness is a contented soul, satisfied with its allotted share and at peace; God grants that richness and enriches in Paradise.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r9.anchor: في الحقيقة إنما هو غنى النفس , وهو رضاها بما قسم لها وسكونها وطمأنينتها , وإنما الله به فهو غني

BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r10.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r10.claim: Al-Baghawi explains aqnā as giving principal wealth and property saved beyond basic needs.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r10.anchor: قال البغوي : أعطى أصول المال وما يدخر بعد الكفاية , قال : وقال الأخفش

BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r11.speaker: الأخفش
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r11.claim: Al-Akhfash instead explains aqnā as “made poor”; al-Isfahani transmits the same view from Abu Zayd and treats the hamza as indicating removal.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p332/r11.anchor: وقال الأخفش أقنى أفقر - انته . ونقل الأصبهاني مثله عن أبي زيد , فتكون الهمزة للإزالة

DURR-FULL:v7p664/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as God giving wealth and contentment.
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى} قال: أعطى وأرضى

DURR-FULL:v7p664/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r2.claim: In another gloss, Ibn Abbas says aghnā means to increase or provide abundantly, while aqnā means to make content.
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أغنى} قال: أكثر {وأقنى} قال: قنع

DURR-FULL:v7p664/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq that God relieves poverty and grants possessions from which a person gains contentment; he confirms the usage with poetry.
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله {أغنى وأقنى} قال: أغنى من الفقر وأقنى من الغنى فقنع به

DURR-FULL:v7p664/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r4.speaker: عنترة العبسي
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas cites ʿAntara's line as Arab usage of aqnā in the sense of being content or restrained.
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r4.anchor: أما سمعت قول عنترة العبسي: فأقنى حياءك لا أبا لك واعلمي أني امرؤ سأموت إن لم أقتل

DURR-FULL:v7p664/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses aghnā as making content and gives a second gloss for aqnā, printed in the source as mūn.
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: أغنى أرضى وأقنى مون

DURR-FULL:v7p664/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r6.claim: Abu Salih explains aghnā as wealth in money and aqnā as stored or acquired possessions.
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r6.anchor: عن أبي صالح في قوله {أغنى وأقنى} قال: غنى بالمال وأقنى من القنية

DURR-FULL:v7p664/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r7.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r7.claim: Qatada and al-Dahhak are reported to give the same explanation as Abu Salih: wealth in money and possessions held as qinya.

DURR-FULL:v7p664/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r8.speaker: الحضرمي
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r8.claim: Al-Hadrami says God is self-sufficient while all creatures depend on Him.
DURR-FULL:v7p664/r8.anchor: عن الحضرمي في قوله {وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى} قال: أغنى نفسه وأفقر الخلائق إليه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3319#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3319#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3319#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the two verbs as “He gave” and “He satisfied.”
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3319#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : اغنى واقنى قال : اعطى وارضى .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p146/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p146/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p146/r6.claim: Provision could have been mentioned before the next creation to move from creation to sustenance, as in two cited passages, but is delayed so the clauses pair God's power over both creations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p146/r6.anchor: إذ ينتقل من نعمة الخلق إلى نعمة الرزق كما في قوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p150/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p150/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p150/r1.claim: The clause occupies the same structural position as the statement that human effort will be seen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p150/r1.anchor: وموقع جملة { وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى } كموقع جملة { وأن سعيه سوف يرى } ( النجم : 40 ) .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r6.claim: Aqnā means to acquire what one keeps; the word also occurs in causative and doubled forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r6.anchor: وأقنى معناه: أكسب، يقال: قنبت المال، أي كسبته، ثم يعدى بعد ذلك بالهمزة، وقد يعدى بالتضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r7.claim: The cited line uses يقنى for acquiring wealth after poverty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r7.anchor: كم من غني أصاب الدهر ثروته ... ومن فقير يقنى بعد إقلال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r8.claim: Some commentators explain aqnā as acquiring things one keeps.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أقنى معناه: أكسب ما يقتني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid explains the phrase as enriching and satisfying.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r10.speaker: حضرمي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r10.claim: Ḥaḍramī says God enriches Himself from need and makes His servants dependent on Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r10.anchor: وقال حضرمي معناه: أغنى عن نفسه وأقنى أفقر عباده إليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r11.speaker: الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r11.claim: Al-Akhfash takes aqnā to mean making poor.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r12.claim: These glosses are not demanded by the word’s language; the author prefers acquiring what one keeps.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r12.anchor: وهذه عبارات لا تقتضيها اللفظة، والوجه فيها بحسب اللغة أكسب ما يقتني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says aqnā means making content; the author praises this since contentment is the best possession and wealth is fleeting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p207#2/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أقنى قنع. والقناعة خير قنية، والغنى عرض زائل، فلله در ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God enriched by granting sufficiency.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r1.anchor: أحدها أغنى بالكفاية قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God enriched by providing livelihood.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r3.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says God enriched through wealth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r4.speaker: سفيان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r4.claim: Sufyān says God enriched by granting contentment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says aqnā means that God made a person content with what He gave.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r5.anchor: أحدها أرضى بما أعطى قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say aqnā means ‘made to serve’; Mujāhid is also reported as holding both this and the preceding view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r6.anchor: والثاني أخدم قاله الحسن وقتادة وعن مجاهد كالقولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says aqnā means that God gave a person a store of property, his capital.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p83#5/r7.anchor: والثالث جعل للإنسان قنية وهو أصل مال قاله أبو عبيدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r5.speaker: أبو صالح وابن جرير وغيرهما
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r5.claim: A common interpretation says God grants people wealth and makes it lasting property they need not sell, completing His favor to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r5.anchor: وعلى هذا يدور كلام كثير من المفسرين، منهم أبو صالح، وابن جرير، وغيرهما.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r6.claim: Mujahid and Qatada interpret aghna as providing and aqna as giving servants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r6.anchor: وعن مجاهد: {أغنى} : مول، {وأقنى} : أخدم. وكذا قال قتادة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid also interpret the words as giving and making content.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد أيضا: {أغنى} : أعطى، {وأقنى} : رضى.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r8.speaker: الحضرمي بن لاحق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r8.claim: Al-Hadrami ibn Lahiq says God made Himself self-sufficient and made creatures dependent on Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r8.anchor: أفقر الخلائق إليه، قاله الحضرمي بن لاحق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says God makes wealthy whom He wills and poor whom He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: {أغنى} من شاء من خلقه و {وأقنى} : أفقر من شاء منهم، قاله ابن زيد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir judges the interpretations that God makes Himself self-sufficient or directly makes some wealthy and others poor to be remote from the wording.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p466#2/r10.anchor: حكاهما ابن جرير (2) وهما بعيدان من حيث اللفظ.

JISHUMI:v9p6667/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع في رواية وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r1.claim: These readers assimilate ʿĀd al-ūlā, omit tanwīn, and do not articulate the hamza distinctly.
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع في رواية، وأبو عمرو، ويعقوب: (عاد لولى) مدغمة غير منونة ولا مهموزة

JISHUMI:v9p6667/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r6.claim: Qinya and qinyān refer to making something a lasting possession; the root denotes keeping something for oneself, while aqnā can mean to give.
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r6.anchor: وأصله: جعل الشيء للنفس على اللزوم، ويقال: قنيت الشيء أقناه إذا لزمته

JISHUMI:v9p6667/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r7.claim: Qanāt is linked to what is kept; its alif derives from wāw and its plural is qanawāt; the text also explains al-aqnā and qanā.
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r7.anchor: ومنه القناة، ألفها واو، وجمعها: قنوات؛ لأنها مما يقتنى، ومنه الأقنى، والقنى: أخذ تراب في الأنف

JISHUMI:v9p6667/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r8.claim: Qanā and iqtanā mean to retain an item for oneself rather than trade it; al-maqniʾa is pronounced with or without hamza.
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r8.anchor: وقنى الشيء واقتناه: إذا أمسكه لنفسه لا لتجارة للزومه له، والمقنؤة مهموزة وغير مهموزة

JISHUMI:v9p6667/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r9.claim: Shade remains attached to what it covers; qān means a lasting red, and aqnā means he gave.
JISHUMI:v9p6667/r9.anchor: والظل: الذي لا تصيبه الشمس، كأن الظل لازم له، وأحمر قان للزوم لونه، وأقنى: أعطى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r17.claim: أقنى means God gave acquired wealth intended to be retained and not relinquished.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r17.anchor: وأعطى القنية وهي المال الذي تأثلته وعزمت

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r14.claim: Aghna means sufficiency, while aqna means increase.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r14.anchor: أغنى بالكفاية وأقنى بالزيادة , وهو معنى قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r15.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r15.claim: Aghna means livelihood, while aqna means wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r15.anchor: أغنى بالمعيشة وأقنى بالمال , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r16.speaker: أبو صالح
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r16.claim: He enriches through wealth and grants qinya, meaning enduring assets or capital.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r16.anchor: أغنى بالمال وأقنى بأن جعل لهم قنية , وهي أصول الأموال , قاله أبو صالح

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r17.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r17.claim: Mujahid glosses the pair as enriching by granting and providing means by withholding.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r17.anchor: أغنى بأن مول وأقنى بأن حرم , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r18.speaker: سليمان التيمي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r18.claim: God enriched Himself and made His creatures dependent on Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r18.anchor: أغنى نفسه وأفقر خلقه إليه , قاله سليمان التيمي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r19.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r19.claim: God enriches whomever He wills and makes whomever He wills poor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r19.anchor: أغنى من شاء وأفقر من شاء , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r20.speaker: سفيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r20.claim: Aghna means contentment and aqna means satisfaction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r20.anchor: أغنى بالقناعة وأقنى بالرضا , قاله سفيان

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r21.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r21.claim: He made a person rich enough not to serve and made others available to be employed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r21.anchor: أغنى عن أن يخدم وأقنى أن يستخدم , وهذا معنى قول السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r22.claim: A further possibility is that God enriches through earnings in life and what a person leaves after death, from the sense of preserving wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p404/r22.anchor: أغنى بما كسبه [ الإنسان ] في الحياة وأقنى بما خلفه بعد الوفاة

MUJAHID:v2p632#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p632#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p632#2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses aghnā as providing wealth.
MUJAHID:v2p632#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ أغنى ﴾ يقول مول

MUJAHID:v2p632#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p632#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p632#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses aqnā as making content or satisfied.
MUJAHID:v2p632#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد

MUQATIL:53:43-50/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:43-50/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:43-50/r6.claim: God enriches a person and makes that person content with what He gives.
MUQATIL:53:43-50/r6.anchor: يقول: مول وأرضى هذا الإنسان بما أعطى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#11/r1.claim: Aqnā means He gave lasting property, wealth a person accumulates and resolves not to part with.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p192#11/r1.anchor: واعطى القنية وهى المال الذى تأثلته وعزمت ان لا تخرجه من يدك

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says God enriches whom He wills and impoverishes whom He wills; al-Tabari chooses this view.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد: أغنى من شاء وأفقر من شاء

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r4.speaker: ابن زيد ومجاهد وقتادة والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r4.claim: They explain aghnā as providing wealth and aqnā as providing servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r4.anchor: وعن ابن زيد أيضا ومجاهد وقتادة والحسن: «أغنى» مول «وأقنى» أخدم

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r5.claim: Another view says God gave people possessions to keep, also linked to providing servants.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets aqnā as making someone content with what God gave after enriching them.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r6.anchor: وقيل: معناه أرضى بما أعطى أي أغناه ثم رضاه بما أعطاه قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r7.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r7.claim: Al-Jawhari says aqnāhu Allah means God gave lasting possessions; it can also mean He satisfied him.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r7.anchor: وقال الجوهري: قني الرجل يقنى قنى مثل غني يغنى غنى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r8.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r8.claim: Abu Zayd says qinā means contentment; Arab usage distinguishes goats as qinā, sheep as wealth, and camels as munā.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r8.anchor: والقنى الرضا، عن أبي زيد قال

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r9.claim: Another usage says God enriched a person and gave what would make them settled.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r9.anchor: ويقال: أغناه الله وأقناه أي أعطاه ما يسكن إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r10.speaker: سليمان التيمي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r10.claim: Sulayman al-Taymi says God enriched Himself and made creatures dependent on Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r10.anchor: أي أغنى نفسه وأفقر خلقه إليه قاله سليمان التيمي

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r11.speaker: سفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r11.claim: Sufyan says God enriches by contentment and grants contentment.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r11.anchor: وقال سفيان: أغنى بالقناعة وأقنى بالرضا

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r12.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r12.claim: Al-Akhfash gives aqnā the sense of impoverishing.

QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r13.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r13.claim: Ibn Kaysan interprets aqnā as giving offspring; al-Qurtubi says this returns to an earlier view.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:47-49/r13.anchor: قال ابن كيسان: أولد. وهذا راجع لما تقدم
